blocks.body: # Premature SILVER Exit Incident and Principal-Protection Fix

## Technical summary

The loss was caused by a policy-ordering defect, not by the take-profit threshold. The `confirmed_reversal` branch returned **exit before checking executable P&L**, so two repeated deterioration readings could authorize a below-cost sale. The position was sold for a realized **$11.8625 loss**; Kalshi later finalized the held YES side.

The production path now has two independent protections: the pure decision policy refuses any sale below all-in break-even, and the execution layer repeats that check immediately before an order can be submitted. Confirmed reversal is disabled by default and remains advisory even when enabled for diagnostics. Ordinary profitable take-profit remains active for both standard scalp and predictor trades.

## The reversal override bypassed a loss calculation that had already said hold

At 5:53:40 PM UTC, the timer evaluation calculated **-$11.8625** of executable P&L and correctly returned `hold/capture`. Roughly 160 milliseconds later, a book-triggered evaluation reused the same 47.69% model reading, advanced the reversal streak to 2/2, and returned `exit/confirmed_reversal` despite the same negative economics. The trigger cited probability, peak drawdown, momentum, and book price. The model and book evidence were uncertain observations—not an authoritative market result.

## The premature sale destroyed $18.4625 relative to settlement

The ledger records an all-in entry debit of **$28.40** for 35 YES contracts. Selling at 49 cents produced $17.15 gross and $16.5375 after exit fees, for **-$11.8625 realized P&L**. Because YES settled at one dollar, holding the same contracts would have returned $35 and produced **+$6.60 P&L**. The difference is **$18.4625**.

## Kalshi finalized YES after the bot had sold

Kalshi's public market record reports `status=finalized`, `result=yes`, a one-dollar settlement value, and a settlement timestamp of 6:00:17 PM UTC. This is the only evidence that made the held side certain; by then there was no reason to sell—the correct lifecycle action was settlement.

## The failure unfolded in under six minutes

- **5:47:58 PM UTC:** bought 35 SILVER YES for $28.40 all-in.
- **5:53:40.197 PM:** timer path held at a 49-cent bid and -$11.8625 executable P&L.
- **5:53:40.357 PM:** a book event reused the same model reading and advanced reversal confirmation to 2/2.
- **5:53:40.472 PM:** all 35 contracts were sold at 49 cents.

## Scope, data, and definitions

The incident population is one production trade: `KXSILVER15M-26AUG251400-00`, trade id `0ecc68ca-915f-48b9-a8d4-83ed80330da3`. **All-in break-even** is original total debit divided by original contracts; this includes entry fees. **Net executable gain** is the held-side bid less estimated exit fee less all-in break-even. **Guaranteed result** means a venue-determined or venue-finalized result, not a model probability, order-book price, strike crossing, or momentum signal.

## The diagnosis reconciled four independent surfaces

The trade and fill rows established realized economics; 466 normalized position evaluations established the policy sequence; the JSONL trace preserved the full reversal reason; and Kalshi's public market endpoint established the later authoritative result. Source was then traced from `TakeProfitExit` through the pure `decide_take_profit` function to the sole live `place_exit_order` boundary used by take-profit. The standard scalper does not have a second position-sale implementation: its open positions are supervised by this shared service.

## Principal protection is enforced before every production take-profit order

- **All-in break-even floor:** negative executable gain always returns `hold/principal_protection`.
- **Order-boundary assertion:** the execution service checks again immediately before `place_exit_order`, so a future policy regression still cannot submit a negative-gain automatic exit.
- **Reversal default:** confirmed reversal is disabled in production and cannot override the profit gates even when enabled for diagnostics.
- **Original cost basis:** partial positions use original contracts, preserving true per-contract break-even.
- **Shared supervision:** predictor and standard scalp positions use the same exit service.
- **Scalp compatibility:** a regression test confirms a scalper still exits when the adaptive net-profit requirements are satisfied.

## Limitations and robustness checks

The $6.60 hold result is a deterministic settlement counterfactual because the position had 35 remaining contracts and Kalshi finalized YES at one dollar. It does not claim that holding every losing-looking trade is generally optimal. Before finalization, no outcome is literally guaranteed; therefore the requested safe behavior means **do not automate a loss sale** and let exchange settlement resolve the binary payoff. The separate legacy salvage feature remains disabled by default and was not involved in this incident.

Incident-specific, standard-scalp, take-profit, mode-switch, and salvage-runtime tests passed. The full regression suite reached 100% with no failures. Targeted Ruff checks on changed Python files passed; a repository-wide Ruff scan still reports pre-existing legacy-code findings outside this change.

## Recommended next steps

1. Start the next live process only from the updated source and verify its startup configuration records `confirmed_reversal_enabled=false`.
2. Monitor `position_evaluations.gate='principal_protection'`; it should produce holds and never a corresponding exit fill.
3. Keep `confirmed_reversal_exit` in the isolated strategy lab until a larger out-of-sample settlement-labeled study demonstrates value; do not restore it as a production loss override.
4. Alert if any future `trade_exit_fills` row yields negative net P&L, because that would indicate an execution/accounting invariant breach.

## Further questions

The next analysis should compare profitable early exits with eventual settlement by asset, entry price, time-to-close, and regime. That can tune the 75% capture threshold without reopening loss exits. It should also measure whether repeated book events carry independent information or merely duplicate one stale model observation, which was a key weakness in this incident.
